newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand delays date for some oil reserve hikes.
newsitem.headline: Thailand delays date for some oil reserve hikes.

text.p: The government board of National Energy Policy Office (NEPO) on Friday decided to delay the deadline for doubling imported gas oil and fuel oil reserves to 1999 from 1997, NEPO Secretary-General Piyasvati Amranand said.
The decision to push back the import hike deadline was made after a request from the commerce ministry, which said increases in reserves for imported oil products could lead to higher inflation.
Piyasvati said reserves on imported refined products other than fuel oil and gas oil will be increased to 10 percent from the current five percent by January 1997 as previously scheduled.

In an effort the ensure sufficient reserves after the Gulf War, Thailand initially raised the reserve requirement for oil products to five percent from three percent of annual oil supply, with a goal to eventually increase it to 10 percent for imported refined product.
The increase was also meant to reduce the advantage importers have over local producers who are currently required to reserve five percent of their crude imports and five percent of oil products.

But the commerce ministry under the present government opposed the plan, saying the increased reserve requirements for imported refined products would lead to higher costs which would be passed to consumers and adversely affect inflation.

"We have to see how much gas and fuel oil local refineries can produce in the next two to three years. If it turns out that we still have to rely a lot on imports, the deadline can be reviewed," Piyasavati said.
During the first eight months of 1996, Thailand imported 176,020 barrels per day of refined products, 100,050 bpd of which was diesel and only 8,510 bpd was gasoline.
